label: copy phase: input in {0,h,i,x,m,1} while outputting m/x/i/h (mid/late recall)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during the original tokens or at <DEL>). The fed-back input is almost always one of a small token set {0,h,i,x,m,1} (99% of activation mass), and the token being output is usually from the same group, mostly m (45% of mass) and x (20%). Almost no activity at recall_idx 0-1. The largest activations come from pairs like input 0/i/x followed by output m, or input m followed by output x (for example ...0 [m] x...). Activations are larger when the next output is also m/x. It does not fire on other inputs such as letters a-g or digits 2-3. Precision is limited: plenty of steps with the right input/output pair stay silent, so magnitude probably depends on more context than this token pair.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: m, x, i, h, 1, 0; least: j, g, c, k) and the current input token, by step (t=13: 0, h, i, x; t=12: 0, h, i, m; t=17: 0, i, h, 1); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, L=9 & t=14, recall_idx=4.
